ticket.title: outfeed install skipped the rebuild silently when the version matched, so source edits never reached ~/.cargo/bin
acceptance_criteria: FIXED 2026-11-06 (outfeed 23207a0). The skip itself was intentional - --force is the documented pre-release mechanism - but it was SILENT and confident: 'up-to-date' reads as 'your build is current' when it means the version string matches
and that cost a debugging detour where the tested binary was two hours older than the source.\n\nTwo changes

per the maintainer's call that both had merit. (1) The skip message now states reason and remedy: 'v0.1.0-beta.7 (up-to-date by version; pass --force to rebuild from source)' - VERIFIED end-to-end by reinstalling outfeed with --force and observing the new text. (2) For --debug installs the version gate is bypassed when any file under the crate's src or its Cargo.toml is newer than the installed binary
because a debug install exists to pick up source edits and those never change the version. Unknowns (no binary
unreadable mtime) resolve to stale: rebuilding unnecessarily costs a minute

skipping a stale binary costs a confusing session. The negative direction is verified (benchwork binary 12:37 vs source 12:30 correctly skipped); the positive direction is not yet exercised.\n\nTier 2: fmt clean
outfeed-core 90/90. Note there are no unit tests on this path - the filtered run reported '0 tests run' - so the behavioural check above is the evidence
